_comment: SPARK — S167: VFX clips for the OWNER-RULED BOSS SKILLS (R138/R139/R140).
⭐ THE OWNER ASKED FOR THESE BY NAME, mid-session: *"also their skills need a generated video or
art (explosion for zombie boss and stinky deadly aura around him)"* and *"we would need to
generate cool graphics for those abilities"*. Only the THREE skill sets he has actually ruled are
here — Pharaoh, Warlord and Archdemon are still his (*"the rest iil think about"*), so nothing is
⛔ THESE ARE EFFECTS, NOT CHARACTERS, AND THAT CHANGES EVERY PROMPT. There is no seed image: an
effect has no identity to hold across states, which is the whole reason the character clips are
image-to-video. What they need instead is ISOLATION — `build-sprite-atlas.mjs` mattes by finding
near-white connected to the frame border, so any ground, scenery or character in frame would be
welded into the cut-out and drawn over the board forever. Every prompt therefore says: the effect
ALONE, on pure white, no background of any kind.
⚠ AND THE SKILLS ARE NOT WIRED YET, DELIBERATELY. `RACE_ZONES_AND_BOSS_TOWERS.md` §S167 costs the
mechanics and finds a real blocker — there is no single place that knows a creature died, so a
death-explosion hook would fire for creature kills and miss tower kills. The ART is generated now
because the owner asked for it and it is the long-lead item; the CODE waits on that design.
⚠ ONE CLIP PER SKILL, played once. None of these loops — an aura that pops back to frame 0 reads
as a stutter, so the renderer will hold or ping-pong it rather than the art being authored to tile.

characters.name: skill-zombie-aura
characters._why: R138 — the zombie boss's damaging aura

cast.prompt: A churning ring of sickly greenish-yellow miasma, low and wide like a disc of gas hugging the ground, boiling outward from a centre point and rolling slowly. Thick, wet, putrid vapour with darker flecks turning inside it, edges curling and dissolving. The effect is shown ALONE on a seamless blank sheet of pure WHITE paper filling the entire frame, with NO character, NO ground, NO scenery and NO background of any kind — only the effect itself, centred, so it can be cut out and drawn over a game board. The camera does not move. The effect plays once, cleanly, from nothing to full and back toward nothing.
